metadata.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

problem.value: Current language representation models are unidirectional, which restricts the power of pre-trained representations and the choice of architectures.

evidence.quote: The major limitation is that standard language models are unidirectional, and this limits the choice of architectures that can be used during pre-training.

contributions.value: Demonstrating the importance of bidirectional pre-training for language representations.

evidence.quote: • We demonstrate the importance of bidirectional pre-training for language representations.

contributions.value: Showing that pre-trained representations reduce the need for heavily-engineered task-specific architectures.

evidence.quote: • We show that pre-trained representations reduce the need for many heavily-engineered taskspecific architectures.

contributions.value: Advancing the state of the art for eleven natural language processing tasks.

evidence.quote: • BERT advances the state of the art for eleven NLP tasks.

method_summary.value: The framework consists of two main steps: pre-training on unlabeled data and fine-tuning using labeled data for downstream tasks.

evidence.quote: There are two steps in our framework: pre-training and fine-tuning.

method_summary.value: The model architecture is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder based on the original Transformer implementation.

evidence.quote: BERT's model architecture is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder based on the original implementation described in Vaswani et al. (2017) and released in the tensor2tensor library.

method_summary.value: BERT is pre-trained using two unsupervised tasks: Masked LM (MLM) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP).

evidence.quote: Instead, we pre-train BERT using two unsupervised tasks, described in this section.

method_summary.value: During fine-tuning, the pre-trained parameters are used to initialize the model, and all parameters are fine-tuned end-to-end on downstream tasks.

evidence.quote: For each task, we simply plug in the task-specific inputs and outputs into BERT and finetune all the parameters end-to-end.

novelty.value: Unlike previous models that use traditional left-to-right or right-to-left language models, BERT uses a deep bidirectional architecture trained with masked language modeling.

evidence.quote: Unlike Peters et al. (2018a) and Radford et al. (2018), we do not use traditional left-to-right or right-to-left language models to pre-train BERT.

novelty.value: Unlike prior work that transfers only sentence embeddings, BERT transfers all pre-trained parameters to initialize end-task models.

evidence.quote: However, in prior work, only sentence embeddings are transferred to down-stream tasks, where BERT transfers all parameters to initialize end-task model parameters.

claims.value: BERT obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks.

evidence.quote: It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5% (7.7% point absolute improvement), MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (4.6% absolute improvement), SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 point absolute improvement) and SQuAD v2.0 Test F1 to 83.1 (5.1 point absolute improvement).
